output.summary: Evidence points to a self-reinforcing loop: agency hours push charge and buddy-orientation duty onto permanent RNs (E5, where load followed agency share in all 7 high-agency units). Exit interviews and the survey cite workload and precepting burden far more than pay (E8, E14). St. Brennan's accounts for only 19 of 98 known destinations (E9). The CFO plan funds the bonus by cutting charge and preceptor differentials while adding preceptor demand (E12). That would worsen the loop, so it is harmful. Extending the 4 West model is preferred, though the earlier pilot null result needs scrutiny. Price versus volume of agency spend, falls, and time-to-hire remain unestablished.
